speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsen with activity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with diplopia on vertical gaze, is very suggestive of a specific neuromuscular condition. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty swallowing recently? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Electrolytes, Creatine_Phosphokinase. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_FMRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results from the blood work and MRI do not show the elevated enzymes or structural abnormalities expected for myasthenia gravis or a tumor; given the specific symptom of diplopia worsening with upgaze and limb weakness improving with rest, I need to assess for ocular and bulbar involvement. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty speaking or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is reassuring; the absence of family history and symmetrical weakness helps narrow the differential. Given the classic fatigue pattern and vertical diplopia, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty chewing/swallowing? REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation, Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody: Present (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The test results showing decreased response on repetitive nerve stimulation and positive acetylcholine receptor antibodies confirm the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
